newsitem.title: USA: MGM goal of increasing EBITDA over $500 mln.
newsitem.headline: MGM goal of increasing EBITDA over $500 mln.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc's President Alex Yemenidjian said the company has set a goal of more than doubling its operating cash flow, or EBITDA, to over $500 million over the next three years from the $250 million in 1996.
Speaking at a Montgomery Securities Hospitality Conference, Yemenidjian said that the EBITDA goal was excluding any expansion into Detroit.
He said that the company was in the process of finalizing its plans about Detroit.

He said the referendum provided for two predetermined licensees for the city and the third license was up for grabs. The company was deciding whether to partner with one of the licensees or bid independently for the third license.
Speaking to reporters after his presentation, he said the company might get the Detroit "request for proposal" (RFP) toward the end of February.

Yemenidjian also said the company saw substantial growth from the planned Atlantic City casino resort and the renovation at the Las Vegas MGM Grand Hotel/Casino. He said the company could use as much as up to $450 million for the two projects from its $600 million line of credit.
Yemenidjian said that Standard & Poor's may raise the company's credit rating from the present BB. "We wouldn't be surprised if the credit rating was raised," he told reporters.
